# Model card: `combined-relative-ridge`

<!-- Generated by `soh train` from the bundle JSON; do not edit by hand. -->

Estimates the state of health (SOH, % of the cell's own initial capacity) of an 18650 Li-ion cell from partial-window health indicators measured during routine operation and divided by the cell's commissioning reference. The capacity itself, or any statistic of a complete discharge, is never an input.

## Model details

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model id | `combined-relative-ridge` |
| Procedure | Ridge regression with nested backward feature selection and penalty choice |
| Exported estimator | median imputation -> standardisation -> ridge (alpha = 1.000) |
| Candidate inputs | feature set `combined` (8) |
| Inputs used | 3: `chg_cv_time_s`, `dis_q_380_350_ah`, `dis_temp_rise_win_c` |
| Mode | relative: each input divided by the mean of the cell's first 5 QC-valid values |
| Output | SOH in %, clipped to [0.0, 120.0] |
| Timestamp (UTC) | 2026-10-12T07:39:55+00:00 (deterministic: the feature table's build time or a fixed config value, not when `soh train` ran) |
| Package version | 2.0.0 |
| Artifact | `combined-relative-ridge.json` (SHA-256 in `MANIFEST.json`) |

## Intended use

- Research and demonstration on laboratory cells like the training cells (2 A constant-current discharge, 24 degC), where a partial charge and/or a partial discharge window is recorded but a full capacity test is not.
- An auditable, leakage-free baseline with battery-level conformal intervals whose coverage is measured on held-out cells, not guaranteed, and an explicit domain-of-applicability check.

## Not intended for

- Safety-critical decisions (charge or discharge limits, thermal protection, warranty or second-life grading). This is not a safety-certified battery-management function.
- Fleet or in-service health monitoring without first validating on the target cells: a handful of laboratory cells cannot establish field accuracy.
- Other chemistries, form factors, temperatures, load currents or test rigs: the training data cover one cell type under one protocol. Inputs outside the training envelope are flagged (`domain.in_domain = false`), but in-range inputs from another population are not detected.
- Remaining-useful-life forecasting: the model estimates current SOH only.

## Training data

- Source: NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence Battery Data Set, cells B0005, B0006, B0007, B0018 (2 A constant-current discharge, 24 degC).
- Rows: QC-valid cycles with a finite label and at least one measured input; reference cycles excluded from fitting and calibration; 612 cycles used for fitting, 24 reference cycles excluded.
- Feature table SHA-256: `f6c4fb709c4810f76a71eaf3ee2b99f963e0fcc94d354dbe636ae8682333d997`.

SOH range of each training cell (fitted cycles):

| Cell | Cycles | SOH min (%) | SOH max (%) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B0005 | 162 | 70.1 | 100.9 |
| B0006 | 162 | 57.3 | 100.0 |
| B0007 | 162 | 74.5 | 100.1 |
| B0018 | 126 | 72.9 | 99.1 |

## Label

`soh_pct` = 100 * capacity / C0; C0 = median of first 5 QC-valid discharge capacities. Capacity enters only the label, never the inputs (enforced by the feature registry and the leakage checks).

## Inputs

| Input | Unit | Availability | Definition | Coef. (SOH pts / SD) | Training range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `chg_cv_time_s` | ratio | partial_charge | Duration of the constant-voltage phase (V >= 4.19 V until current < 0.1 A). | +1.806 | 0.9291 to 1.3507 |
| `dis_q_380_350_ah` | ratio | partial_discharge | Charge delivered while the loaded voltage falls 3.80 V -> 3.50 V (~40% of a discharge). | +12.065 | 0.2744 to 1.0321 |
| `dis_temp_rise_win_c` | ratio | partial_discharge | Cell temperature rise inside the 3.80 V to 3.50 V discharge window. | -0.618 | 0.7778 to 1.1077 |

Prediction = 82.950 + sum of coefficient x (input - training mean) / training SD. A missing input is replaced by its training median and reported as a warning. Contributions are exact (linear model).

## Feature selection

nested backward elimination (battery_soh.evaluation.nested): start from every candidate; repeatedly drop the input whose removal most lowers the inner leave-one-battery-out MAE (penalty re-chosen from the grid at every step); stop when no removal improves it. Penalty grid [0.1, 1.0, 10.0].

Selected on all 4 cells: `chg_cv_time_s`, `dis_q_380_350_ah`, `dis_temp_rise_win_c` (alpha = 1.000, inner LOBO MAE 0.678). Elimination trace:

| Step | Removed | Inputs left | alpha | Inner LOBO MAE |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | (start) | 8 | 0.100 | 1.019 |
| 1 | `dis_r0_ohm` | 7 | 0.100 | 0.994 |
| 2 | `chg_cc_time_390_419_s` | 6 | 0.100 | 0.922 |
| 3 | `chg_temp_rise_cc_c` | 5 | 1.000 | 0.750 |
| 4 | `chg_ica_peak_voltage_v` | 4 | 1.000 | 0.700 |
| 5 | `chg_ica_peak_height_ah_per_v` | 3 | 1.000 | 0.678 |

## Evaluation (leave-one-battery-out)

Source: `reports/benchmark/results.csv`, spec `core_lobo/combined/relative/ridge_nfs`. Each row is a cell the procedure never saw (fitting, selection, penalty and calibration all use the other cells). The shipped model is the same procedure refitted on every cell, so it has no held-out score of its own; these numbers estimate how the procedure does on a new cell of the same population.

| Held-out cell | Cycles | MAE | RMSE | R2 | Bias | 90% coverage | 90% width |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B0005 | 162 | 1.13 | 1.33 | 0.983 | -0.68 | 99% | 4.72 |
| B0006 | 162 | 1.26 | 1.56 | 0.983 | -0.95 | 73% | 3.37 |
| B0007 | 162 | 1.12 | 1.26 | 0.977 | +1.08 | 99% | 6.27 |
| B0018 | 126 | 0.57 | 0.75 | 0.991 | +0.32 | 99% | 3.89 |
| **mean** | 612 | **1.02** | 1.23 | 0.986 (pooled) | -0.06 | 93% | 4.56 |

MAE, RMSE, bias and widths in SOH percentage points; bias = prediction - truth.

## Uncertainty

Method: group conformal (cv): full-data prediction +/- the exact conformal quantile of the pooled leave-one-battery-out absolute residuals over the training cells; each residual comes from a model fitted, selection included, without that residual's cell. Calibration residuals: 612.

| Confidence | Half-width (SOH pts) | LOBO coverage (mean over cells) | Worst cell |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 80% | +/- 1.70 | 81.3% | 46.9% |
| 90% | +/- 1.97 | 92.7% | 73.5% |
| 95% | +/- 2.16 | 96.4% | 87.7% |

Coverage is not uniform across cells. At 90% nominal, B0006 is covered 73% of the time (the model under-estimates its SOH by 0.95 points on average). Even for an exchangeable cell this fixed half-width has no finite-sample guarantee; its coverage is measured, and with 4 cells one unusual cell is enough to pull it far below the nominal level.

B0006 fades to 57.3% SOH, below every other training cell (lowest 70.1%): when it is held out, the model must extrapolate.

## Domain of applicability

An input is flagged out of domain when an indicator leaves its training range widened by 10% of the range, or when its Mahalanobis distance (Ledoit-Wolf covariance of the standardised training inputs) exceeds 3.08, the 99% quantile of the training distances. Out-of-domain estimates are still returned, with a warning.

## Caveats and limitations

- 4 cells from one test campaign of one laboratory. Every metric above averages 4 held-out cells; differences of a few tenths of a point between models are within cell-to-cell noise.
- The label uses each cell's own initial capacity (median of its first five QC-valid capacities), so every cell starts near 100% whatever its nameplate deviation.
- The inputs must be measurable: this model needs a complete CV phase (until the current falls below 0.1 A); a discharge whose loaded voltage starts above 3.80 V and reaches 3.50 V. A missing input is median-imputed and reported in the response warnings.
- The inputs are strongly correlated (they all track the same capacity fade), so individual coefficients, including their signs, are not physical effects; the contributions explain this model's arithmetic, not the cell's chemistry.
- Relative mode needs the cell's own reference values from its first 5 QC-valid cycles in service; without them use an absolute-mode bundle.
- Interval coverage on a new cell is measured, not guaranteed: see the per-cell table.

## Ethical and safety considerations

Over-estimating SOH can keep a degraded cell in service. This model is a research artifact, not a safety-certified battery-management function: do not use it for protection, charging-limit or other safety decisions. Report every estimate together with its interval and domain flag.
